items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: seven years at Cobb's, Cobb's Tea Room... I practically ran that joint because he knew nothing about it... Mr. Cobb loved me, and he should.

ctx.x: I know you must have played in a lot of different kind of places to do that. No.

Four years in Grunewald and seven years at Cobb's, Cobb's Tea Room. Eleven to one at night. We didn't get six sets in. We'd get a beer and get three sets and the night's over. And then when we had competitions with the other places trying to put us out of business, they brought in acts. And Mr. Cobb knew as much about running a nightclub as I knew about flying an airplane. items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: we stayed with Mr. Cobb seven years... Mr. Cobb gave me the music for the luncheon period, the dinner period

ctx.x: Okay. The question was what, about your first band?

I organized my band in 1917. The play at a hotel in Atlantic City. When the war came on, the contract was cancelled. So I played a little jazz at the Orphan Theater, and Mr. Grunlong happened to be in the audience, and he heard us. He waited for me, and he said, they tell me you have a band. I said, yes. He said, could I hear it? I said, let's play him. So we made an audition. We played two numbers.
